description: Compare the chapter's best-singleton and effective-reward-to-truncated-size nonadaptive policies using exact finite distributions.

source.title: Stochastic Knapsack
source.algorithm_attribution: Dean–Goemans–Vondrák nonadaptive approximation: choose the better of the maximum-effective-reward singleton and the nonincreasing w_i/mu_i order.

input.atom_size_rule: For each item, atom size is at most capacity+1.

workspace.meaning: Bounded outcome enumeration, per-item distributions, policy ordering, exact integer scores, and staged output.

contract.independence: Item sizes are independent; each explicit atom weight is a positive integer and is normalized by that item's weight sum.
contract.mean_truncated_size: mu_i = E[min(size_i, capacity)]; valid items require mu_i > 0.
contract.density_order: Nonincreasing w_i/mu_i, compared exactly; equal ratios use increasing item index.
contract.singleton_choice: Maximum w_i, compared exactly; ties use increasing item index.
contract.policy_execution: Process the fixed order until the first item whose realized size would exceed capacity; credit no reward for that overflowing item.
contract.policy_choice: Choose the density order only when its exact expected reward is strictly greater than the singleton's; ties choose the singleton.
contract.output_fraction: Numerator is the weighted expected reward over the full joint atom product; denominator is the product of per-item weight sums; the fraction is not reduced.
contract.error_results: Malformed input returns -1. Null output or insufficient capacity returns -2 without writes.

oracle_method: Enumerate the product of all finite item-size distributions for each candidate nonadaptive policy and compare exact weighted reward numerators over the shared product denominator. The independent verifier uses a capacity-state dynamic program for the density-order policy.
